Cross-attention pooling compression on SmolVLA, LIBERO-Object, 500 eps each:

| M (tokens) | Compression | SR | 95% CI |

- 非单调曲线：M=32/M=64 是甜点（61.6%），M=96 反而更低（52.6%）
- ALL M 值都超过 baseline（44.8%），说明 cross-attention 架构本身有正向作用

- 解读：信息瓶颈效应——适度压缩迫使模型学习更高效表征，过少压缩（M=96）失去正则化收益
- M=128 控制组将决定是否"不压缩 + cross-attention"也有类似效果

SmolVLA exhibits an entropy ratio of 0.98, effectively uniform. The action decoder assigns near-equal weight to all 128 vision tokens, which means that no token is dispensable: each carries an approximately equal share of the information the decoder requires for action prediction. This observation is consistent with the pixel-shuffle analysis above. Because each token already encodes 16 patches, every token is information-dense, and the model has learned to rely on all of them rather than developing selective attention patterns. Under these conditions, pruning any subset of tokens removes a proportional fraction of the decoder's input signal, and the 0\% success rate across all pruning methods and ratios follows directly.

OpenVLA tells a different story. Measured on 250 real LIBERO-Object observations spanning all 10 tasks, its overall entropy ratio is 0.639 ($\pm$0.133), and the layer-wise breakdown reveals progressive sharpening: shallow layers (0\textendash 1) show ratios of 0.98\textendash 0.95, mid layers (5\textendash 16) drop to 0.62\textendash 0.69, and the deepest layers (27\textendash 30) drop further to 0.48\textendash 0.54, with layer 29 reaching a minimum ratio of 0.477. These deep layers, closest to the action prediction head, concentrate the majority of their attention on a small subset of the 256 vision tokens. Only 12.1\% of total attention weight falls on vision tokens overall, and within that fraction, the distribution is highly non-uniform. This pattern indicates that OpenVLA has learned to identify which spatial locations carry task-relevant information and to downweight the rest. Pruning low-attention tokens therefore removes positions that the model already ignores, and the resulting performance loss is proportional to the actual information discarded rather than to the count of tokens removed.
